newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares pare gains in late IBIS trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares pare gains in late IBIS trade.

text.p: German shares advanced strongly in early post-bourse trade on Friday, but fell back in late trade as traders took profits before the weekend, unsettled by a lower dollar.

The IBIS DAX index ended the day up 41.49 points, or 1.3 percent, at 3,288.52 points. The index had earlier risen to 3,313.61 points, but weak early trade on Wall Street and the feeble dollar reined in the index's ascent.
"There's a bit of profit-taking going on this afternoon. The dollar has come off, but the market is so nervous at the moment it's jumping at every new indicator," said one trader.
"The triple-witching just made the market nervous, but it had no real impact except that it will exaggerate the volumes a bit," the trader said.
The volume leader in afternoon share trade was telecoms giant Deutsche Telekom, which was up 1.19 marks, over three percent, at 39.89 marks.

Dealers said the market had been focusing on Deutsche Telekom in recent days as the share, which was floated in November, had been neglected somewhat during the latter record run for DAX blue-chip stocks. "Telecom stocks are in vogue in Europe at the moment, which also helps," dealers said.

Fears of a possible interest rate hike at next week's FOMC meeting in the U.S. contributed to jitters. Comments by Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan on Thursday were interpreted by market players as indicating an imminent hike in U.S. rates.
"A rise of 25 basis points has been discounted by the market, but 50 basis points has not been discounted in and that leaves people around here feeling a little bit vulnerable," a trader said.
The lower Bund future also dampened sentiment in afternoon trade, but dealers said a triple-witching options expiry earlier did not have any major impact on the market.
Also helping boost the stock was a magazine report that the group is budgeting for current year earnings per share nearly 20 percent ahead of existing consensus of analyst expectations.

Shares in steel firm Thyssen AG advanced 16.40 marks or 4.38 percent to end electronic IBIS trade at 390.50 marks on speculation that the company will indeed be the subject of a hostile bid by rival Krupp AG, dealers said.
Krupp and Thyssen have entered talks on a possible merger after Krupp temporarily shelved its takeover offer of 435 marks per share, which it launched earlier this week.
Krupp plans to resurrect its offer if merger talks do not work out. Krupp shares ended up 7.50 marks at 319.50 marks.
